questions.q: What's the fundamental pricing model difference between ADF and Fabric Data Factory?
options: ADF is pay-as-you-go; Fabric is capacity-based (Fabric F SKU)
They use exactly the same pricing model
Fabric Data Factory is entirely free with no billing
ADF only charges for storage, never compute
questions.explain: ADF bills pay-as-you-go per activity run, data movement, and compute, while Fabric Data Factory runs against purchased capacity (an F SKU), which can be shared with other Fabric workloads.

questions.q: Roughly what percentage of ADF activities are currently available in Fabric Data Factory?
options: About 90%
100% — full parity today
About 25%
0% — no activities carry over
questions.explain: Approximately 90% of ADF activities are available in Fabric, plus some Fabric-only additions — but the remaining gap, especially SSIS, can be decisive for some pipelines.

questions.q: Which scenario most strongly points toward staying on classic Azure Data Factory?
options: You run real SSIS packages via the Execute SSIS Package activity
Your destination is already a Fabric Lakehouse
Your organization already owns Fabric capacity for Power BI
You want business users to help build transformations with Power Query
questions.explain: Fabric's SSIS integration story is still undetermined, so pipelines genuinely dependent on SSIS package execution are a strong reason to remain on classic ADF for now.

questions.q: Why might an organization already using Fabric for Power BI lean toward Fabric Data Factory too?
options: Pipelines can run against Fabric capacity they're already paying for
ADF pipelines cannot connect to Power BI at all
Fabric Data Factory is required to use Power BI
There's no real connection between the two products
questions.explain: Since Fabric Data Factory bills against shared Fabric capacity, an organization already invested in that capacity for Power BI can run pipelines against the same purchased resource.

questions.q: Is choosing between ADF and Fabric Data Factory always a strict either/or decision?
options: No — the ADF-item-in-Fabric-workspace path lets organizations run both side by side indefinitely
Yes — an organization must fully commit to exactly one
No — Fabric Data Factory can only ever be temporary during migration
Yes — running both simultaneously is technically impossible
questions.explain: Some organizations deliberately keep SSIS-dependent pipelines on classic ADF while sending new Lakehouse-centric work to Fabric, using the mounted-ADF-item path as a long-term coexistence strategy, not just a migration step.
